verdicts.evidence: I confirmed that none of 'damaged', 'unidentified', 'Gatekeeper', 'SmartScreen' or 'ImageJ' appears in the guide text of /home/user/labconstrictor-site/site/search.json, so the zero-result finding is plausible. docs/guides/install/index.md:155 says only 'If macOS refuses to open it ... Open Anyway'. Config in site/index.html carries 'search.result.none':'No matching documents', so the claim that the empty panel shows no message needs re-checking. AGENTS.md says the build stops when a template page is dropped, so a build failure on a stale heading is consistent with existing practice. I did not re-run the Playwright queries.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Hidden phrases can make a page look like it answers a symptom its visible text does not answer. 'installation failed' pointed at using-apps#something-went-wrong, and 'put my notebook online' pointed at executable-creation, are two examples. Hidden text is also a search-engine spam signal once extra.listed becomes true (it is false in mkdocs.yml now). Heading-keyed entries couple the site build to template and host-repo heading names. The auditor did not verify that highlighting or snippets never expose the hidden words. A Playwright CI check is heavy for a small team.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do S2 first, so the symptom words become visible text in the source repos, then re-measure. Add hidden terms only for true synonyms or proper names of things the section already describes: SmartScreen and Gatekeeper next to their dialogs, ImageJ for Fiji, Mac for macOS. Do not use hidden terms for symptoms the page does not answer. Build it small: data/search_terms.yaml with entries {guide, section, words}, each with a one-line comment naming the visible sentence that justifies it, and about 10 entries in total. Add a short scripts/lcsite/search_terms.py (functions of 30 lines or fewer, annotated, with docstrings) that appends `<span hidden>` at the end of the named section when guides.py assembles the page. The build fails naming file and entry if the guide or heading is missing. Add tests for the failure case and for the span placement at the section end. Add a DESIGN.md 'Search words' pattern first, as AGENTS.md demands. Replace the Playwright CI check with a plain data/search_queries.yaml checklist the maintainer runs by hand before a release. Separately, check in a browser why the empty panel shows no text, because the 'No matching documents' string is already in the page config, rather than adding a new mechanism.

verdicts.evidence: I verified the gap in the built pages and in the template's origin/main. docs/guides/install/index.md:155 has only the 'Open Anyway' sentence. docs/guides/troubleshooting-installed-app/index.md has exactly two sections: the Windows Installed-apps glitch, and the ASN.1 certificate error, written for maintainers (self-test, CA-bundle variables). Its 'uninstalling guide' link points to .tools/docs/download_executable.md, and `git show origin/main:.tools/docs/download_executable.md` begins '### Sorry, but no executable files are available yet'. The local template checkout is on a feature branch that lacks troubleshooting_installed_app.md, so origin/main is the right reference. The template's app/bash_bat_scripts and the unmerged branch origin/claude/uninstall-warning hold the real uninstall behaviour.
verdicts.misleading_risk: The proposal asks for macOS and Linux uninstall steps, a 'how to update an installed app' section, and quoted macOS dialog titles. I found no source in the repos for any of these. macOS dialog wording varies by macOS version. Writing them from memory would put unverified facts into the docs. The Windows Control Panel route is already documented and verified in the page.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Edit LabConstrictor (template) origin/main, .tools/docs only, with facts the maintainers confirm on real machines. (a) troubleshooting_installed_app.md: add short symptom-titled sections 'The app does not open, or the browser stays empty' (point to notebook-usage: the terminal must stay open) and 'macOS will not open the installer'. Put one plain-language sentence above the ASN.1 section and move the self-test and env-var detail below it. (b) install.md macOS step 2: quote the exact dialog text only after a maintainer checks it on a current macOS. (c) executable_creation.md section 3: add one sentence saying where the finished installers are (the repository's Releases page, and the App Centre listing). (d) Fix the dead link by writing one 'How to uninstall' section, or drop the link and state the Windows route inline. Write the macOS and Linux uninstall steps only from the installer's actual behaviour (the uninstall scripts and the branch claude/uninstall-warning). Leave out 'how to update' until someone states what really happens. No change in the site repo, and no README change unless a new file is created.

verdicts.evidence: In built site/search.json, /apps/ holds 2094 characters, /build/ 1585, /guides/ 1525 and /use/ 886, all card copy, so the pollution is confirmed. The auditor's own listing for 'use inside Fiji' was #1 /guides/image-software/ (the host-overview guide, a reasonable answer), #2 /ecosystem/#hosts, #3 /use/. Excluding card grids would remove only /use/ from that list and would not put the Fiji guide first. The auditor admits the end-to-end effect was untested. I found no reference to data-search-exclude in the zensical package files I grepped, and the built site/assets has no match, so the exclusion mechanism rests only on the auditor's scratch build.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Excluding /apps/ card text removes app-name and summary search from the search box. Per-app pages remain searchable, but a query that matched only the list page will now return nothing, so recall can fall as well as precision rising. The change is also not the fix for the 'use inside Fiji' example, which depends on S1 and S4. The pinned Zensical version might stop honouring data-search-exclude.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do the small part first. In scripts/lcsite/hubs.py, wrap the card grids of /use/, /build/ and the Docs home (hubs.write_docs_home) in an element with data-search-exclude, and keep the lead sentence indexed. Add a test that the attribute is present, and a check that search.json holds no text from those grids, so a Zensical upgrade that stops honouring the attribute fails loudly. Leave /apps/ alone for now. Re-run the nine benchmark queries, and add the /apps/ exclusion only if the list page still beats per-app pages for queries like 'what is a notebook'. Record the pattern in DESIGN.md first. Do not count this as the fix for 'use inside Fiji'.

verdicts.evidence: The generic headings are verified in docs/guides/install/index.md (## Windows, ## macOS, ## Linux, ## Next) and in docs/guides/napari, fiji and qupath (## If something does not work, napari line 166, Fiji line 169, QuPath line 166). 'ImageJ' appears in no built guide (grep found nothing). The Fiji section holds a failure dialog, the log path and 'labconstrictor-tools doctor'. The napari section holds the status line, Details, doctor and support-bundle. The QuPath section holds the status line, Details, the log path and doctor. Only one bullet in each concerns registration. I found no inbound link to #if-something-does-not-work outside the three guides.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Retitling the whole section 'My app does not show up in napari/Fiji/QuPath' would misstate its content and hide its real use, which is finding the log and error after a tool fails. The proposed extra bullet 'An app is listed only after you installed it with its installer' is partly supported by the Fiji guide ('The app's installer registers it, which is how the plugin finds it'), but the auditor admits the discovery behaviour is unverified for the other hosts. Renaming a heading changes its anchor, and redirects cannot cover anchors.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep the gap, narrow the change, and do it in the owning repos. (1) LabConstrictor (template) .tools/docs/install.md: '## Windows' becomes '## Install on Windows', '## macOS' becomes '## Install on a Mac', '## Linux' becomes '## Install on Linux'. These are accurate and safe. (2) LabConstrictor-Fiji docs/user-guide.md: write 'Fiji (ImageJ)' in the opening sentence, and the same in LabConstrictor-Tools docs/user-guide.md next to Fiji. 'Fiji is ImageJ' is a safe fact and supplies the visible word that S1 would otherwise hide. (3) In napari, Fiji and QuPath keep '## If something does not work', but make the first bullet a plain symptom line such as 'An app is missing from the list: check that it is installed, then run `labconstrictor-tools doctor`', added only once the host maintainers confirm the discovery behaviour. If a separate section is wanted, add a new short one titled for the symptom instead of renaming this one. (4) Re-run scripts/check_site.py after the rename, since it already fails on dead anchors.
